sourceFacts: Unloaded practice precedes adding external load.
Alternating-lead and static-foot versions are complementary teaching patterns; equal sides and controlled quiet deceleration are emphasized.
A lower platform is appropriate when trunk alignment cannot be maintained; demonstrated box dimensions are not universal starting heights.
appDecisions: Explicit stable-platform and overhead-clearance confirmation, recorded height and independent pattern skill confirmations.
Two-to-four sets of three reps per lead leg, 90-second rest and six-second per-side rep planning estimate. These are configurable app defaults, not #97 numerical prescriptions.
One complete up/down sequence counts as one lead-leg repetition; actual bilateral counts are recorded.
No automatic height or external-load advancement. A configured height change starts a separate comparison cycle; actual height or pattern changes receive no credit against the written setup.
1–100 cm is an input validation range, not a recommended height or universal limit of safe practice.
limits: No automatic loaded step-ups, float variations, taller platforms or additional specialty steps.
The app cannot measure platform stability, actual deceleration, body alignment or overhead clearance. Pain requires stopping/reassessment, not using this lesson as a rehabilitation prescription.

setup: Begin without external load on a stable, non-slip platform that cannot tip. Use a familiar low height that allows controlled stepping; record the actual height in Settings.
Check overhead clearance before the first ascent. The source demonstrates 20/24/30-inch box faces but explicitly says many people need a lower starting step; those are not universal targets.
bracing: Stand all the way up, engage the glutes and control the ribcage and trunk. Lower the platform if you cannot retain controlled alignment.
The transcript does not specify a breathing cadence; do not infer one from the rep counter.
mistakes: Noisy, uncontrolled descent: reduce demand and regain slow deceleration.
Leaning onto the thigh or powering through lost trunk alignment: lower the step instead of increasing height.
Unequal lead-leg practice: record actual counts on each side; extra work on the stronger side does not establish balanced progression.

boxStepUp.purpose: Practice equal lead-leg stepping and controlled ascent/descent before considering loaded or more complex stepping.
steps: Step onto the platform with one lead leg, bring the second foot up and stand fully.
Step down with control rather than dropping noisily.
Change lead and repeat on the opposite side. Count one complete up/down sequence as one repetition for that lead leg; match both sides.

staticStepUp.purpose: Practice controlled stepping while keeping one foot planted, reducing foot-placement variables.
steps: Place one foot on the platform pointing generally forward; keep that foot in the same position throughout the side.
Drive up, straighten the working leg and engage the glute while keeping the trunk controlled.
Lower slowly and use a light toe tap with the trailing foot to regain position. The source also demonstrates a float, but the app does not automatically prescribe that harder option.
Complete the same number of controlled repetitions with the other foot planted.
